title: KYC upgrade rejected three times

customer.name: Chidinma Okafor-Nwosu
customer.account_summary: Wallet 5 months old, wants higher transfer limits for a small business.

messages.text: Good morning. I have uploaded my ID three times now to upgrade my account and it keeps saying rejected. I need my limit raised so I can pay my suppliers. My ID is clear, I don't understand why it keeps failing. Please help.

hidden_root_cause: Chidinma's uploaded ID document shows her legal name as 'Chidinma Okafor-Nwosu' (hyphenated surname, reflecting her married name), while the BVN (Bank Verification Number) record on file shows 'Chidinma Okafor' (unhyphenated, maiden name only). The automated name-matching algorithm scored the match at 78 out of 100, below the 85 auto-approve threshold, causing automatic rejection each time despite the document image itself being clear and genuine.
red_herring: The customer assumes the document image quality is the problem (since it 'looks clear' to her) and keeps re-uploading the same document, which will never fix a name-matching score issue — the fix is a policy override or supporting document, not a better photo.

field_diff.surname: PARTIAL MATCH (Okafor-Nwosu vs Okafor — subset match, hyphenated addition)

knowledge_base.title: KYC name-mismatch override policy
knowledge_base.body: If the automated name-match score is above 70 and the document authenticity check passes, support/compliance may manually approve with a documented override reason (e.g., 'hyphenated married surname, subset match, DOB confirmed'). If the score is below 70, request a supporting document (marriage certificate or affidavit of name change) instead of overriding.

suggested_queries.query: SELECT submission_attempt, match_score, threshold, outcome FROM customers WHERE customer_name = 'Chidinma Okafor-Nwosu' ORDER BY submission_attempt;
suggested_queries.result_summary: Returns 3 identical rows: match_score=78 every time, always below threshold=85 — confirms re-uploading the same document will never change the outcome; the fix is a policy override or supporting document, not a better photo.

root_cause_options.text: Name-match score (78) falls below the 85 auto-approve threshold due to a hyphenated married surname on the ID vs. maiden name on BVN; document image itself is fine.
The document image is blurry or low quality, causing repeated rejection.
The customer's BVN itself is invalid or does not exist in the national database.
Her account is flagged for suspected identity fraud pending investigation.

resolution_options.text: Since match score (78) is above the 70 floor and document authenticity passed, apply a manual override with a documented reason (hyphenated married surname, DOB match confirmed), and escalate to Compliance for override sign-off.
Ask her to re-upload the same ID document a fourth time.
Reject permanently and tell her Tier 2 is not available to her.
Approve unilaterally without any Compliance involvement since the case seems obviously legitimate.

customer_expectation_timeframe: Override decision within 1 business day, or a request for a supporting document if declined
model_reply: Hi Chidinma, thank you for your patience, and I'm sorry for the back-and-forth. I've looked into why your upgrade keeps being rejected: it isn't your document image, which is clear and passes our authenticity check. The issue is that your ID shows 'Okafor-Nwosu' while our records show 'Okafor', so our automated name check can't fully match them on its own. I'm escalating this to our Compliance team with a note explaining the hyphenated married surname and your matching date of birth, so they can manually approve the upgrade. You don't need to re-upload anything for now — I'll follow up within 1 business day with the outcome. If Compliance needs a supporting document (like a marriage certificate), I'll let you know exactly what's required.

root_cause_accuracy.0: Assumed the document image or BVN itself was the problem.
root_cause_accuracy.1: Identified a 'name mismatch' generically without citing the actual score or threshold.
root_cause_accuracy.2: Cited the score/threshold but didn't explain the hyphenated-surname cause.
root_cause_accuracy.3: Correctly explains the hyphenated married surname vs. maiden-name BVN record, and that the 78/85 score — not image quality — caused rejection.

tool_efficiency.0: Did not open KYC Console before responding.
tool_efficiency.1: Saw the rejection but not the field diff/match score detail.
tool_efficiency.2: Saw the match score and field diff but didn't check the override policy KB article.
tool_efficiency.3: Reviewed submission history, field diff, ran the SQL query showing all 3 attempts scored identically (78/85), and read the override-policy KB article before deciding.

compliance_safety.1: Escalated but gave no reasoning/evidence for Compliance to act on.
compliance_safety.2: Escalated with partial reasoning but didn't note the DOB match / authenticity pass.
compliance_safety.3: Escalated to Compliance with a clear, documented override reason and no unilateral limit change promised.
